Adjustable personality

A single frozen smile breaks trust the moment a conversation turns serious, so Phoenix-4.5 shifts between emotional states in real time, showing concern, surprise, curiosity, or contentment while it speaks and listens, and you shape that personality with a few lines of instruction.

Custom actions

A PAL works toward outcomes, not just answers. A system prompt shapes its behavior, objectives give it goals to work through step by step, guardrails set the lines it never crosses, and it can run on Tavus models or your own LLM, so every conversation moves somewhere.

Custom faces

People connect with a face they recognize, so you can build a photorealistic one from a minute of video or a single photo, or pick from a library of 100+ stock faces, which means your PAL can look like you, a teammate, or a brand character.

Custom voices

A voice helps carry identity, so the same minute of video that trains your face reproduces your voice too, or you can choose from the stock voice library or bring one from ElevenLabs or Cartesia, and your PAL speaks 43 languages.

Deploy Anywhere

A PAL is only useful where people actually are, so it goes to them. Invite it to a Google Meet like any teammate, drop it into your site or app with one script tag, or share it as its own hosted page, with nothing to build behind it.

Magic canvas

Magic Canvas lets a PAL bring visuals into a live video conversation, showing a chart, a calendar, a question, or a scheduling page in a panel beside its face. It decides for itself when a card would help, puts it up while it keeps talking, and clears it as the conversation moves. Whatever the person taps or answers flows right back to the PAL and to you.

Presentation mode

Presentation Mode lets a PAL present a slide deck, sharing the slides on screen and talking through them in its own words while it takes questions along the way. You give it a deck from its Knowledge Base, and it can either walk the deck from start to finish or pull up whichever slide fits the moment, so it can lead a full walkthrough or answer from the right slide when someone asks.

Google Meet

A PAL can join a Google Meet as a full participant, on camera, seeing and hearing the room, and taking its turn in real time. You bring it in the way you would anyone else, either by inviting its email to the calendar event or by passing a meeting link through the API, and it joins on its own, even a call that is already in progress.
